goals: Mechanistic: quantify how water partitioning (ET, surface runoff, sub-surface drainage, snow/SWE) varies with elevation across the Bow River headwaters
Validation: check simulated snow and streamflow-relevant fluxes against in-domain observations
key_processes: ET vs runoff vs drainage partitioning

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM is the right tool for point water partitioning, but the domain is outside the forcing coverage that makes the requested elevation signal resolvable.

answerable: Soil-texture control on point water partitioning under a single (non-elevation-resolved) forcing — a conceptual soil sweep, which does NOT answer the elevation question

not_answerable.why: Domain is in Canada (outside CONUS); NLDAS-2 elevation-resolving forcing is unavailable, so the stack falls back to Qian T62 (~1.9°), which is not elevation-resolved. Columns along an elevation transect would receive near-identical precip/temperature, so any gradient would reflect soil, not elevation/climate.
SNOTEL is US-only (absent in Canada); ECCC gauges are not ingested in the stack, and single-column ELM has no routing to produce integrated streamflow for gauge comparison.
not_answerable.needs: in-domain Canadian observation ingest (e.g. ECCC snow/discharge) and runoff routing/aggregation

sampling_strategy.approach: not applicable — primary mechanism not representable
sampling_strategy.n_justification: An elevation-stratified column set is deliberately NOT proposed: with uniform Qian forcing it would isolate soil, not elevation, and would misrepresent the result as an elevation gradient.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: N/A until elevation-resolved forcing exists; would then oversample the rain-snow transition band and valley bottoms.

validation_design.comparison: none — SNOTEL is a US-only network and does not cover Alberta
none — not ingested in stack, and single-column ELM cannot produce routed streamflow

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: none — design blocked by missing elevation-resolved forcing outside CONUS

requires_capabilities.capability: elevation-downscaled forcing with coverage outside CONUS (Canada)
requires_capabilities.why: The elevation signal in partitioning acts through orographic precip and temperature; Qian T62 fallback (~1.9°) is not elevation-resolved and NLDAS is CONUS-only.
requires_capabilities.blocks: The entire primary question — elevation-resolved water partitioning in the Bow River headwaters

requires_capabilities.capability: in-domain Canadian observation ingest (ECCC snow/discharge or equivalent)
requires_capabilities.why: SNOTEL is US-only and ECCC gauges are not in the stack, so no in-domain validation target exists.
Independent 1-D columns produce no integrated streamflow for gauge comparison.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Any streamflow validation against ECCC gauges

assumptions: Domain bbox (-115.6, 50.7, -114.0, 51.4) is entirely outside CONUS/NLDAS coverage, forcing the Qian T62 fallback.
No Canadian forcing or observation dataset is currently ingestible by the stack.
open_questions: Is an elevation-resolved Canadian forcing product (e.g. RDRS, ERA5-Land downscaled) available to ingest? Without it the elevation question cannot be posed to the runs.
Can ECCC snow-course or discharge data be ingested, and is a routing/aggregation step planned to compare against gauges?
Would the user accept a reframed CONUS analog basin (e.g. a US Rockies headwaters with NLDAS + SNOTEL) as a process proxy, clearly labelled as analog rather than the Bow?
